candidates.name: Hemichorea-Hemiballismus
support_spans: Continuous, irregular involuntary movements of variable amplitude were observed in the left arm and leg.
Noncontrast CT of the head showed slightly increased density in the bilateral striatal regions without evidence of acute infarction.
Subsequent brain MRI demonstrated high-signal intensity on T1-weighted images in the bilateral basal ganglia.
candidates.why: The patient's symptoms and imaging findings are consistent with Hemichorea-Hemiballismus, a movement disorder characterized by involuntary movements and abnormal signal intensity in the basal ganglia on MRI.
